root_cause.text: Race condition in netfilter counter reset where concurrent dump-and-reset operations could read the same counter values before either subtracts them, causing double subtraction and counter underrun.
root_cause.evidence: Commit message explicitly states "preventing concurrent dump-and-reset from underrunning values" and "two parallel resets cannot both read the same counter values and then both subtract them." The patch adds a global spinlock (`nft_counter_lock`) around the fetch-then-reset sequence in the new `nft_counter_fetch_and_reset()` function, and only uses it when `reset` is true, ensuring atomicity of the read-and-subtract operation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add spinlock to synchronize control plane fetch and reset of nft_counter data to avoid race conditions.
intent_record.what: Added a static spinlock `nft_counter_lock` with a comment indicating it is for control plane sync fetch+reset.
intent_record.how: The new spinlock `nft_counter_lock` will be used to protect control plane operations (e.g., fetching and resetting counters) from concurrent access, preventing data races against per-CPU counter state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing counter reset on dump by implementing fetch-and-reset under spinlock when reset flag is set.
intent_record.what: Added a new function nft_counter_fetch_and_reset that atomically fetches and resets counter values under a spinlock, and modified nft_counter_do_dump to call the new function when the reset parameter is true, otherwise call nft_counter_fetch as before.
intent_record.how: When nft_counter_do_dump is called with reset=true, the counter values are now fetched and then reset atomically under a spinlock, ensuring correct state after a dump; previously the reset parameter was ignored.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove counter reset from dump operation to avoid unintended side effects when reading counter values.
intent_record.what: Removed the conditional reset of the nft_counter (if reset flag is set) inside the nft_counter_do_dump function, which was called after successfully dumping the counter values.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the counter will no longer be reset when a dump request includes a reset flag. Previously, the counter values were dumped and then immediately reset; now the dump only returns the current values without modifying the counter.

Resets counter by subtracting the fetched total from per-CPU values outside any lock, allowing another concurrent dump-and-reset to also subtract the same initial values, causing counter underrun.

vuln_statements.explanation: Fetches per-CPU counter values without holding any lock, creating a race window where concurrent dump-and-reset operations can read the same initial values before they are subtracted, leading to double counting and counter underrun.

Resets counter by subtracting the fetched total from per-CPU values outside any lock, allowing another concurrent dump-and-reset to also subtract the same initial values, causing double subtraction and counter underrun. This operation should be atomic with the fetch under a spinlock.

Author: Pablo Neira <pablo@netfilter.org>

    netfilter: nft_counter: rework atomic dump and reset
    
    Dump and reset doesn't work unless cmpxchg64() is used both from packet
    and control plane paths. This approach is going to be slow though.
    Instead, use a percpu seqcount to fetch counters consistently, then
    subtract bytes and packets in case a reset was requested.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces a new mechanism: nft_counter_fetch now uses seqcount to consistently read per-CPU counters without resetting, and nft_counter_reset subtracts the total from the current CPU's counter. The old cmpxchg64-based reset inside the fetch loop (which caused the race) is removed. Thus the vulnerable construct is absent and the fix is present.

Author: Pablo Neira <pablo@netfilter.org>

    netfilter: nft_counter: rework atomic dump and reset
    
    Dump and reset doesn't work unless cmpxchg64() is used both from packet

    Instead, use a percpu seqcount to fetch counters consistently, then

bic_trace_step.reason: The nft_counter_reset function only subtracts the fetched total from the current CPU's counter (lines: this_cpu->packets -= total->packets; this_cpu->bytes -= total->bytes;), but the total is the sum across all CPUs. Concurrent dump-and-reset operations on different CPUs will both fetch the same total and each subtract it from their own CPU, causing double subtraction and counter underrun. The seqcount ensures consistent reads but does not prevent this race. Thus, the vulnerable construct of double subtraction is still present.
